title: Statistics - Lesson 8: Conditional Probability Practice
description: Practice identifying restricted denominators and solving conditional probability from tables, Venn diagrams, and short contexts.

questions.question: In the expression P(A | B), which event gives the denominator?
options: Event A, the event being asked about
The event outside both A and B
The full sample space every time
questions.explanation: In P(A | B), B is the given condition. The denominator is restricted to outcomes in B.

questions.question: A class survey shows 24 learners attended review. Of those, 18 passed the quiz. What is P(passed | attended review)?
questions.explanation: The condition is attended review, so use 24 as the denominator and 18 as the favorable count.

questions.question: Simplify: If 9 of 15 learners in the given group chose robotics, what is the conditional probability? Enter a simplified fraction.
questions.explanation: The given group has 15 learners and 9 chose robotics, so 9/15 simplifies to 3/5.

questions.question: In a Venn diagram, 7 learners are in both music club and honor roll. There are 20 learners in music club altogether. What is P(honor roll | music club)?
questions.explanation: Music club is the given group, so the denominator is 20. The overlap with honor roll is 7.

questions.question: P(A | B) and P(B | A) always have the same value.
questions.explanation: They use different denominators unless A and B have the same size or a special relationship.

questions.question: A bag has 5 red and 3 blue counters. One red counter is removed and not replaced. What is P(second counter is red | first counter was red)?
questions.explanation: After a red counter is removed, 4 red counters remain out of 7 total counters.

questions.question: Explain in one sentence why the phrase "among students who passed" changes the denominator.
questions.correctAnswer: It restricts the sample space to only the students who passed, so the denominator is the number of students who passed.
questions.explanation: Conditional probability uses only the group named by the given condition.

questions.question: If P(A and B) = 0.21 and P(B) = 0.70, what is P(A | B)? Enter a decimal.
questions.explanation: Use P(A | B) = P(A and B) / P(B). Then 0.21 / 0.70 = 0.30.
